8581.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰalós, traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *bʰelH- (“to shine”), with cognates including Sanskrit भाल (bhāla, “splendour”), Old Armenian բալ (bal, “fog”), Old English bǣl (English bale), and, in particular, Lithuanian bãlas…

8578.t: τέμνω (témnō, “to cut”) + -ος (-os). Hypothetically inherited from Proto-Hellenic *tómos, from Proto-Indo-European *tómh₁-o-s, from *temh₁- (“to cut”).

8574.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰembʰ-; compare Old Armenian դամբան (damban, “tomb”).

8502.t: Back-formation from ταὐτό (tautó, contraction of τὸ αὐτό (tò autó), neuter nominative singular), and equivalent contractions in other cases and genders.

8539.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tréhō, from Proto-Indo-European *tréseti. Cognates include Latin terreō, Old Irish tarrach, and Sanskrit त्रसति (trasati).

8518.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téukʰō, a thematicized formation from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéwgʰti, root present of *dʰewgʰ-.

8585.t: Contraction of φαεινός (phaeinós), from Proto-Hellenic *pʰawehnós, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰh₂wesnós, adjective noun from substantive *bʰéh₂wos (whence φάος (phắos)), from *bʰeh₂- (“to shine”).

8575.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téretron, from Proto-Indo-European *térh₁trom, from the root *terh₁- (“to rub away at; to bore, drill”). By surface analysis, τετραίνω (tetraínō, “to bore”) + -τρον (-tron).

8528.t: Oriental foreign word of unknown origin.

8560.t: From τροχάνη (trokhánē, “wheel, axle, gear”) + -τήρ (-tḗr), from τροχάζω (trokházō, “to run quickly”).

8531.t: Maurice connects τυλυφάντης (tuluphántēs, “cushion-cover weaver”), assuming influence of κορύνη (korúnē) or τορύνη (torúnē) to account for the vocalism. Furnée compares Luwian [script needed] (taluppi, “clump of dough”).

8579.t: From a *bʰ-extension of Proto-Indo-European *dʰewH- (“mist, smoke, haze”). Compare also τῦφος (tûphos, “fever”), τυφόω (tuphóō, “delude”), Τυφῶν (Tuphôn, “Typhon”).

8591.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰey- (“to decline, disappear”). Cognate with Sanskrit क्षिणाति (kṣiṇā́ti, “to destroy, ruin”), English dwindle, Spanish sed (“thirst”), French soif (“thirst”).

8588.t: φειδός (pheidós) + the same suffix found in ἁμαρτωλός (hamartōlós, “sinful”).

8557.t: By surface analysis, τρόμος (trómos) + -έω (-éō). However, it may also derive from Proto-Hellenic *troméyō, from Proto-Indo-European *troméyeti, a causative from *trem- (“to tremble”) + *-éyeti.

8512.t: From τετρακοσιοστός (tetrăkosĭostós, “four hundred”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).
